additional_requirements: manic_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) is characterized by a continuous period of illness during which a major mood episode (manic or mixed, and often depressive as well) occurs concurrently with symptoms that meet Criterion A for schizophrenia. To qualify, there must also be at least two weeks of psychotic symptoms in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, distinguishing it from mood disorders with psychotic features. The course is typically chronic or relapsing, with variable levels of functional impairment, and may include periods of relative stability between episodes. It is differentiated from schizophrenia by the prominence and duration of mood episodes, and from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features by the persistence of psychosis outside of mood episodes.

patient.personality: Fred is a friendly, down‑to‑earth handyman who enjoys being the reliable helper in his Midwestern community, splitting his time between odd jobs, outdoor hobbies, and relaxed social gatherings.
patient.stressor: About sixteen months ago, Fred had to stop working regularly after a minor cardiac event led his doctor to recommend significantly cutting back on physically demanding jobs, which abruptly shifted him from a busy, go‑to fixer in the neighborhood to someone with long, unstructured days at home. Losing his role as the dependable handyman and community volunteer left him feeling restless and unsure how to define himself, and he began throwing himself into home projects, community activities, and new plans to "finally get everything done" around the house and garage. Over the next year and two months, this restless drive escalated, with Fred taking on more and more simultaneous projects, becoming increasingly disorganized in his routines, and neglecting bills and basic self‑care, which created tension with his wife and concern among friends who noticed he was no longer his usual steady self. When a neighbor found him exhausted, agitated, and surrounded by half‑finished, overly ambitious projects he insisted he had to complete immediately, his wife persuaded him to see a psychiatrist to understand what had changed.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like I’ve got this nonstop engine in me, I’m going from one project to the next and can’t seem to slow down.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Lately I’ve been convinced the city and the hospital are keeping tabs on me because of my heart and all these projects, like when I see the same white pickup drive past the house twice I’m sure they’re checking on what I’m building in the garage, even though my wife keeps telling me it’s just a coincidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: Pretty often, especially late at night in the workshop, I hear a man’s voice plain as day calling my name or telling me things like “finish the plan” or “they’re watching,” even when I’m alone and the TV and radio are off.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.
S021.manifestation: My wife and friends say it’s hard to follow me because I’ll start out talking about fixing a neighbor’s fence, then suddenly I’m on about how the power company is wasting energy and how I should design a new kind of generator, and I don’t really notice I’ve jumped tracks until they give me that confused look.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: I’ll get so wound up that I’m pacing from the basement to the garage to the backyard, picking things up and putting them down, starting to hammer or measure something and then dropping it to go rearrange the shed or draw on the walls like I’ve got to do everything at once and can’t just sit still or follow a normal routine.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Most days I either feel cranked way up and on top of the world, snapping at my wife if she even hints I should slow down, or I’m suddenly irritated at little stuff like the neighbor’s dog barking, like my mood has a short fuse and flips on a dime.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: Ever since I had to cut back on work it’s like a switch flipped and I can’t stop moving, so I’ll be up on a ladder, then tearing apart the lawnmower, then reorganizing every drawer in the kitchen, all in the same afternoon, and I still feel like I haven’t done enough.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I catch myself telling people I’ve figured out a new way to redo half the houses on our block, or that I could run the whole neighborhood better than the council, like I’m the only one who really sees how everything should work and it just seems obvious to me in the moment.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: There are stretches where I only sleep three or four hours a night because I’m up sketching plans or puttering in the garage, and even though I know I should be tired, I wake up feeling wired and telling my wife I don’t really need sleep like other people do.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My mind feels like a bunch of power tools going at once, with ideas about fixing the roof, starting a community garden, writing a book about my life, and figuring out how the government is watching our neighborhood all crashing into each other so fast I can’t slow any of it down.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: I’ll be halfway through fixing a cabinet hinge and then a bird flies past the window or I hear a car door slam, and suddenly I’ve dropped the screwdriver and wandered off to start mowing a patch of lawn or sorting screws in a coffee can, forgetting what I was doing in the first place.
